transcript:
This message comes from Angie. Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled pros
to get their home projects done well for over 30 years. For everything from minor repairs
to major remodels, find reviews, pricing, and booking at Angie.com or on the Angie app.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder. A tight race with no clear winner, exit polls suggest
neither Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, nor the center-right opposition led by former
military chief of staff, Gadi Eisenkopf, have a clear path toward a governing majority after
Tuesday's elections. But do not, Arbelle says she feels optimistic. We feel really hopeful.
We've had four hard years. We haven't left the streets every Saturday night. We've been on the
streets fighting for Israel, fighting for this country that we love so much. We want a bright,
pink future here. Arbelle joining Israelis on the streets of Tel Aviv Tuesday night. If no
block wins a majority, it could take days or weeks to decide who will be Israel's next Prime Minister.
The Trump administration is moving to overturn a Biden-era climate regulation on methane emissions
at oil and gas wells. NPR's Kirk Sigler reports on the president's announcement while he was
campaigning in Texas Tuesday night. President Trump is proposing to rescind a 2023 Biden-era
rule that aimed to reduce emissions of methane, a major contributor to climate change, and 80 times
more planet heating than carbon dioxide. This regulation requires oil and gas companies to
monitor for leaks at drilling sites and to dramatically cut emissions. Trump's EPA
administrator Lee Zeldin says these regulations were "unworkable" for the industry and predicted
the rollback would spur more domestic drilling and ultimately save billions in production costs.
In a statement to NPR, the American Petroleum Institute said the EPA's proposed reconsideration
is a step toward addressing technical challenges behind implementing the Biden-era rule.
Kirk Sigler, NPR News. President Trump is back in the nation's capital after rallying Republican
voters in Texas. He held two rallies there Tuesday in support of GOP Senate candidate Ken
Paxton's campaign against Democrat James Talarico. Elon Musk has invested heavily in
defeating Talarico, making the race one of the most expensive in the country.
The Federal Election Commission's electronic filing system remains down just a week before
Election Day. Officials say they're investigating what happened as NPR's Ashley Lopez reports.
The FEC is an independent agency that regulates campaign finances in elections. It does not play
any role in administering elections, though, so this outage does not affect any of voters' ability
to cast a ballot. However, the agency does keep record of how much money campaigns are raising
and spending, especially this last week of voting, which has the highest spending days for campaigns.
According to the FEC, campaigns are currently unable to use online web forms like the Electronic
Filing System for Campaign Finance reports. The broader FEC website, however, is currently
working. Ashley Lopez, NPR News.
Tampa Bay Rays still in it. The Rays staved off elimination from the World Series Tuesday
night with a 12th inning rally, beating the Milwaukee Brewers 4-3 and forcing Game 5 and
the best of seven. This is NPR. The U.S. says it will issue visas to Flavio Bolsonaro and his family.
Bolsonaro lost Sunday's presidential election runoff in Brazil and is under investigation
on corruption charges. Here's NPR's Carrie Khan.
According to a U.S. administration official, the State Department will issue visas to Bolsonaro
and his family, allowing entry into the U.S. In a video released Monday, Bolsonaro said federal
police officials had ordered him to surrender his passport. He's facing multiple investigations,
including allegations of money laundering and tax evasion. He has denied any wrongdoing.
The U.S. has not recognized the results of Sunday's presidential election won by incumbent
Luis Inacio Lula da Silva. Trump did not endorse Bolsonaro, a close conservative ally,
but he has said the Brazilian elections appeared "rigged." Carrie Khan, NPR News, Rio de Janeiro.
Authorities say they have connected serial killer Ted Bundy to the death of a Utah teenager. The
announcement Tuesday comes exactly 52 years after the body of 17-year-old Melissa Ann
Smith was discovered. Authorities say DNA connections between Smith and another Bundy victim
helped close the case. Bundy was executed in 1989. Stocks in Asia rallying Wednesday trading ahead of
an interest rate decision by the Federal Reserve. They're getting a boost from AI-related stocks.
South Korean shares up more than 6 percent. Japan's Nikkei is up 1.3 percent. The Fed expected to
leave interest rates unchanged when policymakers wrap up their meeting Wednesday. This is NPR News.
This message comes from Rosetta Stone. Rosetta Stone is designed to make language learning

write, and think in a second language. More at RosettaStone.com.

Tel Aviv voter Arbelle says she feels hopeful after four years of protests
Trump administration proposes rescinding Biden-era methane emissions rule for oil and gas wells
Trump rallies Republican voters in Texas backing Ken Paxton against James Talarico
FEC electronic filing system remains down one week before Election Day
Tampa Bay Rays beat Milwaukee Brewers 4-3 in 12 innings, forcing World Series Game 5
U.S. to issue visas to Flavio Bolsonaro and family after his Brazilian election loss
